Contributing to illume

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thanks for considering it. This file says what the project expects, so that a contribution is not turned away for a reason nobody told you.

Reporting a bug

Open an issue with a reproducible example — the smallest script that shows the problem, with set.seed() if it involves simulation, plus the output of sessionInfo().

If the bug is that a model gives the wrong answer, say what you compared it against. That is not a formality: every defect this package has had was found by comparing against an outside implementation or by widening a simulation, and none was found by the test suite. A report that says “illume gives 0.42 and glmmTMB gives 0.51 on this data” is worth more than a long description.

Proposing a feature

Open an issue before writing code. Two questions get asked of anything new:

  1. Does it need a new hard dependency? The answer has to be no. A package in Suggests, used behind requireNamespace(), is fine.
  2. If it is a diagnostic, what remedy does it name? Every check in this package names a fix that exists in this package. A diagnostic that reports a problem and leaves the user to find the answer elsewhere is a complaint, and will not be merged as one. Where the remedy did not exist, it was built first.

Making a change

  • Branch from main, one change per pull request.
  • devtools::document() after touching roxygen. Committed man/ must match.
  • devtools::test() must pass. The suite takes about half an hour.
  • devtools::check() must be clean. CI runs it on Linux, macOS and Windows against R release, devel and oldrel.
  • Match the surrounding code: ilm_ prefix on exported functions, en-GB spelling, comments that say why rather than what.

Claims and evidence

A statement about how the package behaves belongs in studies/, not in a sentence. If a change alters a number that appears in the documentation — a coverage rate, a timing, an agreement tolerance — the study that produced it is re-run and the generated findings file is updated with it. Findings are generated by studies/scripts/summarise_run.R and are never hand-written.

Do not commit raw .rds output from a study run. .gitignore excludes it, and the study scripts use fixed seeds so it can be regenerated exactly.

Using generative AI

Permitted, and disclose it. Say in the pull request which tools you used and what for. You are responsible for reviewing and validating anything they produced, and for the design decisions either way.

This is not a rule imposed on contributors from outside it: the package itself was drafted in collaboration with a language model under human direction, and says so in the README. The standard asked of a contribution is the standard the package holds itself to – that a claim about behaviour comes with a measurement, and that the measurement is against something somebody else wrote.

Code of conduct

By participating you agree to abide by the code of conduct.

Questions

Open an issue. There is no mailing list.
